🪟 एक बेईमानी के बाद दूसरी बेईमानी आसान क्यों हो जाती है?

कल्पना कीजिए...

एक इमारत की एक खिड़की टूट गई।
किसी ने उसे ठीक नहीं किया।

🧱 कुछ दिनों बाद दूसरी खिड़की भी टूट गई। दीवार पर कोई लिख गया। सड़क पर कचरा पड़ा रहने लगा।

अब वहाँ रहने वाले लोगों को एक संदेश मिल रहा है:

_“यहाँ किसी को परवाह नहीं है।”_

*यही विचार ब्रोकन विंडोज़ इफ़ेक्ट के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हुआ।*

👥 1982 में जेम्स विल्सन और जॉर्ज केलिंग ने तर्क दिया कि किसी जगह पर दिखने वाली छोटी-छोटी अव्यवस्थाएँ लोगों को यह संकेत दे सकती हैं कि यहाँ नियमों की निगरानी कमजोर है।

और जब लोगों को लगता है कि कोई नहीं देख रहा, तो छोटे नियम तोड़ना आसान हो सकता है।

लेकिन यहाँ एक महत्वपूर्ण बात है।

*इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि:*
“एक टूटी खिड़की अपराध पैदा करती है।”

🔎 बाद के शोधों में इस सिद्धांत के कई हिस्सों पर बहस हुई है। अपराध और अव्यवस्था के पीछे गरीबी, संस्थागत कमजोरी, बेरोज़गारी और सामाजिक परिस्थितियों जैसे कई कारण हो सकते हैं।

फिर भी इसका एक सवाल हमारे रोज़मर्रा के जीवन में बहुत गहरा है।

🗑️ अगर सड़क पर पहले से कचरा पड़ा है, तो क्या हमें भी कचरा फेंकना थोड़ा आसान लगता है?

🚶 अगर पूरी लाइन में लोग नियम तोड़ रहे हैं, तो क्या हमें भी नियम तोड़ना उतना गलत लगता है?

🏢 अगर किसी जगह में छोटी बेईमानी को लगातार नजरअंदाज किया जाता है, तो क्या बड़ी बेईमानी के लिए भी भीतर प्रतिरोध कम हो सकता है?

लेकिन ब्रोकन विंडोज़ इफ़ेक्ट का गहरा सवाल केवल सड़क की टूटी खिड़की से नहीं, हमारे भीतर से शुरू होता है।

बाहर की टूटी खिड़की कहती है:
“यहाँ किसी को परवाह नहीं है।”

🪞 *लेकिन भीतर की टूटी खिड़की?*

एक बार झूठ बोला।
एक बार बेईमानी की।
फिर उसे सही ठहरा दिया “सब करते हैं।”

🔄 *अगली बार वही करना थोड़ा आसान हो गया।*

क्यों?

क्योंकि अब अहंकार को सिर्फ गलत काम नहीं बचाना है, अपने पुराने चुनाव से बनी हुई अपनी पहचान भी बचानी है।

🔄 एक गलत चुनाव के बाद उसी दिशा में दूसरा गलत चुनाव करना आसान, और उससे पलटना मुश्किल होता जाता है।

एक चुनाव के बाद अगला चुनाव अक्सर उसी “मैं” को बचाने के लिए होता है।

समस्या केवल यह नहीं कि मैंने क्या किया।

❓ असली सवाल है:
_“वह काम मेरे भीतर के किस केंद्र से निकला था?”_

यही ईमानदारी से देखना है।

❓ *आप ऐसी कौन-सी जगह पर नियम सिर्फ इसलिए मानते हैं क्योंकि वहाँ कड़ी निगरानी रखी जाती है?*

UPI’s zero-MDR era has effectively ended for a segment of merchant payments.

The UPI Steering Committee has fixed MDR at 40 bps for merchant transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The fee is payable by merchants, while payments up to ₹2,000 remain free.

At 40 bps, the ecosystem could generate up to ₹16,000 crore annually. Moneycontrol’s analysis shows transactions above ₹2,000 account for only 2.5% of UPI transactions but nearly ₹6 lakh crore about 67% of merchant UPI value.

That makes the policy significant not because it affects most UPI payments, but because it targets the relatively small slice carrying a disproportionate share of transaction value.

'Targeting 15% ROE as We Scale Up Loan Book'

Q&A with Pankaj Gadgil, MD & CEO, Aditya Birla Housing Finance — on growth targets, portfolio mix, AI and efficiency

Growth Outlook — Next Two Years
Target: AUM of ₹1 lakh crore over next 8–10 quarters — implies CAGR of 25–40% depending on timeline (two to two-and-a-half years)

Targeting 15% ROE with ROA reaching ~2.4%

Focus on maintaining asset quality and improving profitability while scaling

Key Levers for Growth
Currently 209 points of sale — adding minimum 100 branches this year (67 already launched)

Added ~1,000 employees — employee base now ~5,900

₹2,750-crore capital infusion from Advent International sufficient for next 18–24 months as AUM moves towards ₹1 lakh crore

If CAGR maintained at 35–40%, additional capital will be required after two years

Incremental borrowing of ₹20,000–22,000 crore needed as AUM moves from ₹48,000 crore to ₹68,000–70,000 crore

Borrowing & Liability Profile
Will continue to diversify liabilities

NCDs account for ~45% of liability profile

Term loans 32%, NHB funding 12%, short-term funding 11%

Portfolio Mix — Prime, Affordable & Construction Finance
Decided to remain a full-stack player

Current mix: Prime 47%, Affordable 38%, Construction Finance 15%

No significant change expected — Prime could move to ~45%, construction finance to remain at 15–16%

Within affordable housing, lowest-ticket informal-income segment currently ~6% of portfolio — expected to rise to ~11% over next 8–10 quarters

AI — 22 Use Cases in Housing Finance
Currently 22 AI use cases in housing finance — 13 live spanning:

Acquisition, underwriting, portfolio management

Customer service, sales coaching

Software development, audit and compliance

Objective: improve productivity even as capacity is added

Efficiency Gains from Technology
Cost-to-loan-book ratio declined from 2.93% at end of FY25 to ~2.21%

Ambition: bring this down to 1.7% over next 8–10 quarters

Technology, digital and AI critical to achieving that

AI Impact Across Aditya Birla Capital
Health insurance: AI processes nearly 74% of cashless claims; 35%+ of pre-authorisation requests processed straight-through

Life insurance: 100% of new-business processing is digital; ZARA bot collected ~₹411 crore in renewal premium during Q1 FY27

Agentic voice bots: enabled 90%+ first-call resolution; generated ₹1,500+ crore in impact across renewal premium, GMV and AUM

Mutual funds: Disha platform contributed to 12% incremental portfolio creation

Next Big Focus Area in AI
Building an enterprise-wide knowledge layer so data created for one use case can be used across others

Also focusing on ontology and semantic layers, data engineering and APIs

I have watched two birds
leave the same branch
in opposite directions,
each carrying a little morning
inside its wings.
The branch did not follow.
It simply trembled awhile
beneath the weight
of what had been there.

Love comes like that..
without asking whether the season is kind,
without consulting distance or tomorrow.
It places its whole, unreasonable tenderness
into our ordinary hands
and calls that faith.
For a while, someone becomes the lamp
left burning in the kitchen
after every other room has gone dark,
and even loneliness forgets its old name.

Then the weather changes.
Not cruelly.
Only as weather does.
A road bends where neither heart expected.
A season asks more
than two people can give
and still remain gentle.
And suddenly you are learning
how to become separate
without becoming strangers.

Yet the body keeps its small knowledge:
how they liked the window open,
how much milk went into their coffee,
which silence meant stay,
the almost invisible tiredness
that entered their voice before sleep.
Morning comes,
and all that knowing wanders the rooms
like a dog no one has told
the door will not open again.

I used to call this failure.
I was wrong.
Some loves come as rain
to a field that has forgotten rain..
brief, 
complete,
already disappearing into the earth
while the roots beneath
are only beginning to wake.
The rain does not remain
to witness what it has changed.

Years later, 
something greens.
Perhaps only a tenderness
you cannot remember learning,
the way you now hold another person's sorrow
without trying to repair it,
the mercy with which you forgive
what once would have hardened you.
And somewhere beneath your ribs
there is still a small room
where winter enters
but cannot finish its work.

So if love finds you
in tall grass,
at an airport,
across an impossible distance,
or barefoot in an ordinary kitchen,
go toward it.
Do not ask the sky
to swear it will never change.
The sky has other work.
Love does not become more true
because it survives every season.

And if one day you must open your hand
around the one
you once believed you would keep,
open it gently..
as you would release a living bird
back into the enormous field.
Not because holding it meant nothing.
Not because leaving makes the love less real.
But because sometimes the last tenderness
we can give what we love
is not to turn our love into a cage.

Then let them go.

The hand will remember the warmth.
The branch will remember the weight.
The field will remember the rain.

Someone walks away.
The longing does not.

It stays
the way evening light stays trembling on water
after the bird
has disappeared beyond the trees..

not asking to be called forever,
not asking to be understood,

only shining
where something beautiful
once passed.

THE COLLATERAL MIGRATION — PART 7 OF 7

The Nation That Banks on Anklets

Divide the vault book by the average pledge: ₹3.3 lakh crore across ₹1.96 lakh average loans. Roughly 17 million pledges outstanding. Seventeen million households, each with metal in a locker standing surety for cash in a kitchen.

The supply side answered. Aditya Birla Capital — which entered gold loans only this August — is building a thousand dedicated branches over three years. The pawn counter is now on the tier-2 and tier-3 high street — next to the sweets shop, staffed, compliant, air-conditioned.

And the system stays calm. The RBI's Financial Stability Report projects bank bad loans below 2% through 2028. Household debt has climbed to 45.5% of GDP. Read those together: the banks are clean because the stress has been moved into the households. The shock absorber of the Indian economy is now the family balance sheet.

This is the mirror of everything this series has shown. China's households hoard gold — self-insurance against the state. India's households pledge it — self-insurance against the market. Korea's borrow against future income. Across Asia, the family is the residual claimant of every shock the system doesn't want.

Seven parts of The Collateral Migration: the boom, the rulebook, the margin call, the kitchen, the border, the silver frontier — and now the nation they compose. Not a country with a gold problem. A country whose households quietly became its credit system, its food security and its shock absorber, one pledge at a time.

SME Emerge - What it means ⤵️

NSE Emerge and BSE SME are dedicated platforms that enable small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to raise capital and get listed on the stock exchanges.

SME companies are generally smaller in size than companies listed on the main boards and may be at an earlier stage of their growth journey.

SME listings can provide investors an opportunity to study businesses with potentially large growth opportunities, particularly in niche or emerging sectors.

However, SME stocks can also have lower liquidity, higher volatility and greater business risks than established main-board companies.

Investors should therefore pay close attention to financial performance, cash flows, debt, corporate governance, valuations and promoter quality.

For long-term investors, the SME segment can be viewed as a universe for research and tracking, rather than assuming every listed company will become a successful investment.

Bottom line:

For years, we could think:

Weak rupee = Good for IT.

That equation is no longer enough.

The market has stopped asking how many extra rupees IT companies earn from every dollar.

So the rupee at Rs. 95 still helps.

But think of it as a painkiller, not a cure.

Currency can support reported earnings.

It cannot solve weak demand.

And there’s one number that shows how much has already changed.

The five biggest IT companies now make up less than ~7.6% of Nifty 50.

At their peak in the early 2000s, the sector's weight was above 20%.

Then add another problem: the US.

Nearly 57% of the sector's revenue comes from there.

So IT is simultaneously dealing with slower client spending AND questions around what AI does to future pricing.

That matters because Indian IT traditionally grew by adding people as clients added projects.

AI can change that equation.

A project that earlier needed 100 engineers may eventually need far fewer people with AI doing part of the work.

And AI is now the bigger question.

Indian IT was built around a simple model:

Global companies need technology work → outsource it to India → Indian IT earns the difference.

Now AI is asking an uncomfortable question:

What if the same work needs fewer people?

Here’s the easiest way to understand it.

A weak rupee can make flat dollar revenues look better when converted into rupees.

But it cannot create new clients.
It cannot create new projects.

And it cannot protect an old business model from AI.

And for years, markets rewarded exactly that.

Weak rupee?

Investors looked towards TCS, Infosys, Wipro and other IT exporters.

But 2026 has broken that relationship:

Rupee: past Rs. 95/$ Nifty IT: ~29% down YTD

So clearly, something bigger is overpowering the currency benefit.

The old logic was actually quite simple.

Indian IT companies earn a large part of their revenue in dollars but report profits in rupees.

So when $1 moved from Rs. 80 → Rs. 85, the same $1 billion of revenue became more rupees.

A weak rupee was an automatic cushion.

For years, Indian investors knew one simple rule:

Rupee falls → IT stocks benefit.

But in 2026, the rupee has crossed Rs. 95/$… and Nifty IT is still down ~29%.

posts.text:
今日かなり気になった
インド×RWA×中央銀行マネーのニュースです👀

インドというだけで
少し遠い市場に見えるかもしれませんが・・・
今回の話は
 「証券をトークン化しました」だけではありません

インド証券取引委員会
SEBI が
約6200億ドル規模の社債市場を背景に
Demat 2.0
という実証を始めました

まず数字だけ見ると・・・
「6200億ドルの社債が全部オンチェーン化？」
と思ってしまいますが
そこは違います

市場全体
↓
約6200億ドル規模

今回の初期実証
↓
 1025クロールピー
＝102.5億ルピー

です

参加したのは・・・
・REC
・Larsen & Toubro
・IIFL Finance
の3社
なので現段階では
まだパイロットです

それでも今回
私が一押ししたい理由は・・・
証券だけではなく
「支払うお金」まで同じデジタル基盤へ載せたこと
です
ここがかなり大きいです

RWAやトークン化証券では・・・

社債
↓
トークン化

株式
↓
トークン化

ファンド
↓
トークン化

という話をよく見ます
でも・・・
証券だけ速く動いても

代金の支払いが・・・

銀行送金
↓
営業時間待ち

照合
↓
確認

決済
↓
後から

では
取引全体は
まだ完全にはデジタル化されません

そこでインドが今回使うのが・・・
デジタルルピー
です

しかもこれは
USDT
USDC
のような民間ステーブルコインではなく
インド準備銀行
RBIが発行する中央銀行デジタル通貨
です

流れを見ると・・・

トークン化社債
↓
投資家へ移転

同時に・・・

デジタルルピー
↓
売り手へ移転

そして
両方成功した時だけ取引成立
という仕組みを使います

これが
アトミックDvP
です

DvPは
Delivery versus Payment
日本語では
証券の受け渡しと
代金の支払いを連動させる仕組み
です

簡単にすると・・・

証券だけ渡った
↓
でもお金が来ない

お金だけ払った
↓
でも証券が来ない

これを防ぐために・・・

証券
＋
お金
↓
同時に交換
します

今回さらに面白いのは
その「お金」の側が
中央銀行マネーだということです

つまり・・・

トークン化証券
×
中央銀行デジタル通貨
を
同じ決済工程へ載せています

ここまで来ると
「ブロックチェーンで社債を発行しました」
より・・・
資本市場の決済インフラそのものを
作り替えようとしている
と見る方が近い気がします

そしてインドの設計は
既存金融を全部捨てて
新しい暗号資産市場を作る
という形でもありません

むしろ・・・

既存の証券口座
↓
残す

KYC
↓
残す

証券預託機関
↓
残す

既存の取引基盤
↓
残す

その裏側で・・・

所有記録
決済
利払い
償還
↓
分散型台帳へ接続

していきます
ここも重要です

最近のRWAニュースを追っていると
「ブロックチェーンが既存金融を置き換える」
というより・・・
既存金融のバックエンドへ
ブロックチェーンが入り込む
動きが増えています

今回のインドは
そのかなり分かりやすい事例です

もう一つ気になったのが
法的な所有権を誰が持つのか
です

今回トークン化されても・・・
社債の

・ISIN
・利率
・満期
・格付け
・契約条件
・投資家権利
は
そのまま維持されます
そして正式な所有記録も
引き続き
インドの証券預託機関が担います

つまり・・・
「暗号資産っぽい新商品」を作った
のではなく
既存の社債そのものを
新しい記録・決済方式へ移す
という設計です
ここは
前に見たSECの移転代理人の話とも少し似ています

トークンを作れる
↓
だけでは足りない

誰が正式な保有者？
↓
必要

誰が記録する？
↓
必要

代金はどう払う？
↓
必要

決済はいつ確定？
↓
必要

です

さらに・・・
投資家自身が
秘密鍵を管理する必要もありません

預託機関
↓
鍵を管理

投資家
↓
既存に近い証券口座で利用

という形です
なので・・・
ブロックチェーンを使う
＝
全員がウォレットと秘密鍵を自分で管理
でもありません

ここは機関投資家には
かなり大きいと思います
そして今回
個人的に一番気になったのは・・・
証券とお金が
初めて“同じ時間軸”へ近づいたこと
です

これまで・・・

トークン化債券
↓
24時間動ける

でも・・・

決済用の銀行マネー
↓
営業時間や既存決済網に依存

となると
最後のお金のところで
止まる可能性があります
ところが・・・

社債
↓
デジタル化

銀行マネー
↓
デジタルルピー

両方
↓
同時決済

となれば
資産とお金を
同じデジタル時間軸
へ載せられる可能性があります

これはRWA市場では
かなり大きなテーマです

たとえば今後・・・

トークン化国債
↓
24時間

トークン化社債
↓
24時間

トークン化ファンド
↓
24時間

でも

支払いのお金
↓
止まる
なら

市場全体は
24時間にはなりません

だから・・・
資産のトークン化
だけでなく
決済資産のデジタル化
も必要になります

インドは今回
そこをセットで試し始めました

今後は・・・

第2段階
↓
流通市場

個人投資家
↓
拡張

第3段階
↓
参加ノード・対象商品の拡大

が検討されています

なので見るべきなのは・・・
「6200億ドル市場！」
という大きな数字だけではなく
102.5億ルピーの実証が
本当に二次流通へつながるか
です

そして・・・

大量取引
↓
耐えられる？

障害
↓
どう復旧？

サイバー攻撃
↓
どう対応？

利払い
↓
自動化できる？

償還
↓
安定して処理できる？

個人投資家
↓
使える？

ここが次の確認ポイントです
インドのニュースは
日本では少し注目されにくいですが・・・

今回については
「社債をトークン化した」
ではなく
「証券と中央銀行マネーを
同時に動かす資本市場を試し始めた」
と見ると
かなり見え方が変わると思います

RWAの次の競争は
何をトークン化した？
から・・・
「資産とお金を
どう同時に決済する？」
へ進んでいるのかもしれません

今日はここ
かなり注目しています👀

எல்லோரும் இதை atomic settlement என்றும், பணம் உடனடியாக கைக்கு வரும் என்றும் கொண்டாடுகிறார்கள். இதுவரை ஒரு பாண்ட் விற்றால் பணம் வர 2 அல்லது 3 நாட்கள் ஆகும். இப்போது smart contracts மூலம் உடனே நடக்கும் என்கிறார்கள். ஒரு பக்கம் இது முன்னேற்றம் போல தெரிந்தாலும், இன்னொரு பக்கம் யோசித்தால் இது ஒரு விதமான பதற்றத்தை உருவாக்கும். 

REC, L&T மற்றும் IIFL ஆகிய மூன்று நிறுவனங்கள் சேர்ந்து 1,025 கோடி ரூபாய் வரை இந்த பைலட் திட்டத்தில் திரட்டியுள்ளன. IIFL மட்டும் 1 முதலீட்டாளரிடம் இருந்து 25 கோடி ரூபாய் வாங்கியிருக்கிறது. இந்த வேகம் பெரிய நிறுவனங்களுக்கு வசதியாக இருக்கலாம். ஆனால் ரீடைல் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் உள்ளே வரும்போது, யோசிக்க கூட நேரமில்லாமல் எல்லாம் நடப்பது ஆபத்தானது. 

தவறுதலாக ஒரு டிரான்சாக்ஷன் நடந்தால் அதை சரி செய்ய கால அவகாசம் இருக்காது. CBDC wallet மூலம் e-rupee-யில் பணம் செட்டில் ஆகும் என்கிறார்கள். டெக்னாலஜி வளர வளர மனிதர்களுக்கான பாதுகாப்பு குறைகிறதோ என்று தோன்றுகிறது.

ஆனாலும் நான் சொல்வது தவறாக இருக்கலாம். ஏனென்றால் இந்த சிஸ்டம் மூலமாக தேவையில்லாத பேப்பர் ஒர்க் குறையும். ரிஜிஸ்ட்ரார் பாண்ட் ஹோல்டர் லிஸ்ட் எடுத்து ஒவ்வொன்றாக செக் செய்ய வேண்டிய அவசியம் இல்லை. எல்லாம் தானாக நடக்கும்போது எர்ரர் குறைய வாய்ப்பு இருக்கிறது.

उसी नंबर से मेरे दो रिश्तेदारों को Recovery के लिए कॉल कैसे हुई?

एक 15 साल की बच्ची से Recovery के नाम पर कथित रूप से गाली-गलौज क्यों की गई?

John 14:8–9 does not say Jesus is God.

Philip asks Jesus, “Lord, show us the Father,” and Jesus replies, “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.” In context, Jesus is explaining that he perfectly represents and reveals the Father—not saying that he is literally the same person as the Father.

In fact, the same Gospel repeatedly distinguishes Jesus from God:

Jesus says, “The Father is greater than I.” (John 14:28)

He also says, “This is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” (John 17:3)

And after his resurrection: “I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.” (John 20:17)

As for Revelation 1:8, the speaker is identified as “the Lord God… the Almighty”, not explicitly as Jesus. The surrounding passage distinguishes “God” from “Jesus Christ” (Revelation 1:1–2).

Revelation 1:17–18 says, “I am the First and the Last… I was dead, and behold I am alive forevermore.” This is indeed spoken by the risen Jesus in the passage. But saying Jesus has a divine title or attribute is not the same as Jesus explicitly saying, “I am God.” That is the theological conclusion that Christians draw from the text.

So again, let’s distinguish between what Jesus explicitly says and what later theology concludes from certain titles and passages.

Jesus explicitly calls the Father “the only true God” (John 17:3) and calls the Father “my God” (John 20:17). Those statements deserve to be considered alongside the passages being presented as proof of Jesus’ divinity.

2030: The End of the Company
By 2030, one of the most fundamental assumptions of modern society may begin to disappear: the idea that people must belong to a company in order to work.
AI agents, robotics, automation, cloud computing, and blockchain are transforming far more than productivity. They are challenging the very structure of the modern organization—a system in which people gather inside permanent institutions, managers supervise employees, and companies coordinate human labor.

A new model is beginning to emerge.

Instead of massive, permanent organizations, humans and artificial intelligence may form temporary, purpose-driven networks. Organizations may appear when a mission requires them, operate autonomously with AI, and disappear once their purpose has been fulfilled.

The company is not an eternal institution.

Just as money, governments, and industries have evolved throughout history, the concept of the company may now be approaching its next great transformation.

This book explores not only the future of jobs, but something far more fundamental:

What happens when the organization itself begins to disappear?

2030 may not be the year every company vanishes. But it could become the moment when humanity realizes that society may no longer require the traditional company to function.

What will humans do when they no longer need to belong to an organization to create value?

And what kind of civilization will emerge after the company?

This is not simply a book about the future of work.

It is a book about the future of human organization itself.

India’s Bond Market Goes Onchain🔥

Demat 2.0 is not just Demat upgraded. It is finance becoming programmable.

SEBI and RBI’s Demat 2.0 pilot tokenises corporate bonds on a permissioned DLT network, while the e-Rupee handles the cash leg.

The important part is not simply speed.

Bond + money can move simultaneously, reducing settlement risk, reconciliation and layers of back-office intermediaries.

More importantly, the bond itself becomes programmable. Smart contracts can eventually automate interest payments, redemptions and other servicing, turning a traditionally paperwork-heavy process into software.

And tokenisation changes the economics of access. As the system scales, bonds can potentially be fractionalised into smaller units, making an asset class historically dominated by institutions accessible to retail investors.

The pilot has already processed over ₹1,025 crore, involving issuers such as REC, L&T and IIFL Finance.

But this is bigger than corporate bonds.

India is effectively testing the rails for an onchain financial market, with the same infrastructure potentially extending to equities, funds, gold and other real-world assets.

NSE Eyes Revenue Diversification Beyond Options Trading; Has Not Applied to Market Regulator for Permit to Trade Shares on Own Exchange

The IPO Details
NSE IPO scheduled to open for public subscription on September 17

Complete OFS of 126.4 million shares priced at ₹1,700–1,785 per share

Issue size pegged at over ₹22,500 crore at valuation of around ₹4.42 trillion at upper end of price band

Anchor investments on September 16; public bidding September 17–21

NSE shares will list on BSE with 100% free float after six months

All pre-IPO investors will have a six-month lock-in period

NSE has no promoter — fully owned by the public; after first six months will have 100% free float

Revenue Concentration — The Risk
In FY26, 90% of total revenue is operating revenue; within that 60% comes from options

Within options breakdown: 46% from index options, 6% from monthly index options, 8% from single stock options

In monthly options and single stock options, market share is close to 100%

Key risk highlighted by Samco Securities' Equity Research Analyst Raj Gaikar: nearly four-fifths of revenue is transaction charges while three-quarters of that is options

MD & CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan: "Now other businesses are coming up and hopefully we will be able to even further diversify"

Diversification Strategy
Expansion of commodity segment and growth in exchange-traded funds (ETFs)

Emergence of Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs) — Sebi framework to bring retail investors into equity derivatives as a better way of managing risk

"Our innovation is going to be a form of investment. As the country evolves, as the market policy evolves, we are going to get more demands from market participants"

New growth drivers: SIFs, commodities and ETFs

Motilal Oswal Financial Services noted in its IPO note: expansion in diversified product portfolio such as electronic gold receipts, 10-gram gold futures, Brent crude oil futures, electricity futures and Indian natural gas futures

On Closing Auction Session (CAS)
Chauhan: "There have been many times when Sebi has taken measures which the industry thought were tough — and kind of opposed those measures. Later on, it was found that because of those measures more people came to the market because more people thought it was safe"

1/ On 11 Sept 2026, Metropolitan Stock Exchange put
out a press release.

Its Electronic Bond Platform had handled a tokenised
corporate bond for IIFL Finance under SEBI's new
Demat 2.0 pilot.

Arranger: Trust Investment Advisors.

Remember that name. 🧵

2/ The release reads like a milestone.

SEBI Chairman and RBI Governor launching the pilot
at Global Fintech Fest. Distributed ledger. CBDC
settlement. India's first tokenised bonds.

If you hold MSE shares, this looked like the news
you'd waited a decade for.

3/ So let's start with what an EBP actually is.

Any private placement of debt securities of ₹20 cr
or more MUST route through a registered Electronic
Book Provider. It's mandatory.

There are four: NSE, BSE, MSE, NSDL.

MSE has held this licence since 2016.

4/ Ten years with the licence.

FY26 operating revenue: ₹3.4 crore

FY26 net loss: ₹25.8 crore

NSE did ₹25,785 cr within two months of launching
in 2016. Today it holds ~95% of the debt RFQ market.

So what went wrong?

5/ Not the licence. MSE always had permission.

Bond issuance runs on relationships. An arranger who
trusts you. An ops team that answers at 9 PM when a
bid file breaks.

That takes people. People take money.

Nobody funds a bond desk on ₹3.4 cr of revenue.

6/ And Demat 2.0 doesn't fix that.

The ledger belongs to the depositories.

The cash rail belongs to RBI.

The exchange runs the bidding screen.

MSE got a better back office. So did NSE and BSE.

The same day.

Tokenisation is not a moat.

7/ So we stopped reading press releases and opened
MSE's private placement filings.

Jan 2025: ₹238 cr. Groww's parent, Rainmatter
(Zerodha), Securocrop, Share India.

29,75,00,000 shares each. Exactly equal.

Aug 2025: ₹1,000 cr offered to 29 offerees.

8/ ₹1,238 crore total. Roughly 365x annual
operating revenue.

And read those 29 names — it stops looking like a
venture round.

Monarch Networth. Marwadi Chandarana. KIFS. Findoc.
Excel. Achintya. StockGro. Mansi Share.

A broker consortium with a venture fund attached.

9/ Then we got to number fourteen on the list.

Trust Investment Advisors Private Limited, BKC.  The same arranger from the press release in tweet 1.  

Equity offered August 2025. Deal delivered September 2026.  

10/ That one line item is the whole story.  

MSE didn't win that deal on technology ,NSE and BSE got the identical rail on the identical day.  

It won because someone in the bond market finally had a reason to pick up the phone.  That's what ₹1,238 crore actually bought.  

11/ The honest caveat:  

The mechanism has worked exactly once. One arranger. One deal. ₹25 crore. One investor.  MSE's slice of the ₹1,025 cr pilot was 2.4%.  

A real signal. 

Not a turnaround.  

12/ Full breakdown

Not a whitepaper. Not a sandbox demo. Actual money from actual issuers.

And here's what should make every RWA person sit up.

The money hits the issuer's account the SAME DAY bidding closes. That used to take two to three days. The bond and the cash move together on one ledger, so both clear or neither does.

Coupons and redemptions go on smart contracts next. Then secondary trading. Then retail.

Every RWA project on earth has spent three years pitching tokenized bonds to institutions that won't return their calls. India just shipped it with a central bank doing the settlement.

The pilot is small. The number behind it isn't.

#NSDL LAUNCHES DEMAT 2.0 FOR TOKENISED SECURITIES AND CBDC SETTLEMENT

National Securities Depository Limited has launched Demat 2.0, a next-generation platform that supports tokenised securities and enables near-instant settlement through the Reserve Bank of India's wholesale Central Bank Digital Currency.
The initiative forms part of a joint SEBI-RBI pilot for tokenised corporate bonds, unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey.
In an interview at the event, an NSDL official described Demat 2.0 as the next step after the original dematerialisation system introduced about 30 years ago. Demat 1.0 replaced physical share certificates with electronic records. This improved settlement speed, reduced disputes and built greater trust in the market. Settlement cycles gradually shortened from several days or weeks to the current T+1 cycle, with optional T+0 available in some segments.
Demat 2.0 extends that framework. It operates on a blockchain platform and uses two linked wallets: a securities wallet that holds the tokens and a currency wallet that holds the wholesale CBDC (digital rupee).
Under the process, an issuer creates bond tokens. Investors subscribe and successful bidders receive allocation. The tokens are credited to the investor's Demat 2.0 account. Simultaneously, the corresponding CBDC amount is transferred in an atomic delivery-versus-payment mechanism. The investor parts with money and receives the securities at the same moment. There is no time lag between the two legs of the transaction.
This instantaneous settlement reduces settlement risk compared with the existing system, where a gap remains between payment and delivery. The official compared the difference to that between NEFT and IMPS, or to the speed of UPI.
The platform is currently in pilot mode and limited to bond tokens. Later stages are expected to add trading capabilities and expand to other instruments, subject to regulatory approvals and market maturity. Investors continue to use their existing demat accounts and KYC. No separate account is required.
Corporate actions such as interest payments and redemptions can be automated through smart contracts under applicable rules.
Tokenised bond issuances by REC Limited, Larsen & Toubro Limited and IIFL have already raised a combined Rs 1,025 crore on the distributed ledger platform.
The official noted that several Western markets still operate on T+2 settlement for conventional securities, with Europe preparing to move to T+1. India, he said, has consistently led in introducing market infrastructure innovations in a regulated manner and remains in a leading position with this development.
Demat 2.0 retains the legal structure, investor rights and regulatory safeguards of the existing demat system while adding atomic settlement and tokenisation capabilities.

Here is what you need to know about this game-changing upgrade:

🔹 The Trial is Already Live: Three major institutions—REC Limited, Larsen & Toubro (L&T), and IIFL Finance—have already successfully issued a combined ₹1,025 crore (~$116 million) in tokenized bonds under the new framework.

🔹 Atomic Settlement: By connecting tokenized securities to the RBI's wholesale Central Bank Digital Currency (wCBDC), the system introduces Atomic Delivery-versus-Payment (DvP). The bond and the cash move instantaneously—either both settle together or neither does, entirely removing traditional counterparty and settlement risks.

🔹 Smart Contract Automation: Coupon payments and bond redemptions are encoded directly into the tokens, paving the way for automated asset servicing and eliminating massive back-office reconciliation friction.

🔹 Seamless UX: For investors, there is no need for crypto wallets or new accounts. Demat 2.0 works as a native extension of existing regulated demat accounts, with statutory depositories securely managing the private cryptographic keys.

US vs Indian Solar: What’s the real issue?

The US is challenging India’s solar subsidies and has proposed duties of 125.87% + 123.04% on Indian solar imports. Final decision is still pending.

India exported around 4.5 GW of solar modules in FY26, with the US taking the majority of those exports.

Simple example: if an Indian company sells a solar panel in the US for  Ra 100, these duties can make that panel far more expensive there. Buyers may simply look for panels from other countries.

That means Indian manufacturers could have more panels looking for buyers in India. More supply, tougher competition and lower selling prices can hurt profit margins.

Stocks to watch, from higher to lower export exposure:

🔴 Waaree Energies: ~21% overseas revenue
🟠 Vikram Solar: ~16% exports
🟡 Saatvik Green Energy: limited export exposure
🟡 Solex Energy: limited export exposure
🟢 Premier Energies: ~0.8% exports
🟢 Emmvee: primarily domestic

The interesting part is that not all of them are equally exposed to the US. Some have already shifted towards the domestic market, while Waaree has been building manufacturing capacity in the US.

So don’t just see “US tariff = all solar stocks down.”

The real question is: Who actually sells to the US, who manufactures there, and who will be left fighting for the Indian market?

India launches Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenized corporate bonds

SEBI and the RBI have launched Demat 2.0, a regulatory-sandbox pilot testing Indian corporate bonds as native digital tokens on a private, permissioned ledger.

The bonds retain their existing ISINs, coupons, maturities and investor rights, while ownership is recorded by statutory depositories NSDL and CDSL. Settlement uses the RBI’s wholesale digital rupee, enabling atomic delivery-versus-payment.

Three issues totaling ₹10.25 billion (approximately $110 million) have already been completed by REC, L&T and IIFL Finance. The pilot currently focuses on institutional issuance, with secondary trading and retail access planned for later stages.

The project is not a new asset class or public crypto product. It tests whether tokenized bonds can improve settlement, automate coupon payments and reduce reconciliation within India’s existing regulated market infrastructure.

SEBI और RBI ने मुंबई में आयोजित ग्लोबल फिनटेक फेस्ट के दौरान संयुक्त रूप से 'Demat 2.0' का पायलट प्रोजेक्ट सफलतापूर्वक लॉन्च किया है. यह भारत के पूंजी बाजार  के इतिहास में एक क्रांतिकारी कदम है, जो हमें CBDC के उपयोग के बेहद करीब ले आया है।

Demat 2.0' क्या है और यह कैसे अलग है?

Demat 1.0 (1996): इसने कागजी शेयरों (Paper Shares) को डिजिटल डेटाबेस में बदला था।

Demat 2.0 (2026): यह Blockchain या Distributed Ledger Technology  पर आधारित है,इसके तहत कॉरपोरेट बॉन्ड्स  को डिजिटल टोकन के रूप में जारी किया जा रहा है।

CBDC (Wholesale e₹) से इसका सीधा कनेक्शन
Demat 2.0 का प्लेटफॉर्म RBI के थोक CBDC नेटवर्क से जुड़ा हुआ है।
एटॉमिक सेटलमेंट : इसका मतलब है कि जैसे ही निवेशक को डिजिटल बॉन्ड टोकन ट्रांसफर होगा, वैसे ही उसी पल पैसे का भुगतान CBDC वॉलेट के जरिए हो जाएगा. पहले सेकेंडरी मार्केट में फंड और सिक्योरिटी ट्रांसफर होने में 2 से 3 दिन का समय लगता था, जो अब रियल-टाइम हो जाएगा।

स्मार्ट कॉन्ट्रैक्ट्स' का जादू (ऑटोमैटिक ब्याज)

CBDC और DLT के इस मिलन से सबसे बड़ा फायदा यह होगा कि बॉन्ड पर मिलने वाला ब्याज (Coupon) और मैच्योरिटी का पैसा किसी इंसान या बैंक मैनेजर द्वारा ट्रांसफर नहीं किया जाएगा।

इसमें Smart Contracts (कोडिंग निर्देश) लिखे गए हैं, जैसे ही भुगतान की तारीख आएगी, सिस्टम अपने आप निवेशक के CBDC वॉलेट में पैसा क्रेडिट कर देगा ।
इस पायलट प्रोजेक्ट की शुरुआत REC Limited (₹500 करोड़), L&T (₹500 करोड़), और IIFL (₹25 करोड़) द्वारा टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड जारी करके सफलतापूर्वक कर दी गई है, भारत दुनिया का पहला ऐसा देश बन गया है जिसने अपनी मौजूदा कानूनी मार्केट व्यवस्था के भीतर ही टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड्स और देश की आधिकारिक डिजिटल करेंसी (CBDC) के सेटलमेंट को एक साथ जोड़ दिया है।

Demat 2.0' के लॉन्च होने के बाद आम रिटेल निवेशकों  के लिए यह व्यवस्था कैसे काम करेगी और भविष्य का रोडमैप क्या है?
पायलट प्रोजेक्ट के सफल परीक्षण के बाद, इसे आम रिटेल निवेशकों के लिए खोल दिया जाएगा. जब यह आपके और हमारे लिए लाइव होगा, तब इसमें भाग लेने की प्रक्रिया बेहद आसान होगी।
आपको कोई नया डीमैट अकाउंट खोलने या नए सिरे से KYC कराने की जरूरत नहीं होगी,आप अपने मौजूदा डीमैट अकाउंट से ही इन डिजिटल टोकनाइज्ड बॉन्ड्स को खरीद सकेंगे

आपको अपने डिपॉजिटरी (NSDL या CDSL) के जरिए 'Demat 2.0' सर्विस को एक्टिवेट करना होगा और अपने बैंक खाते के साथ एक Wholesale CBDC (ई-रुपया) वॉलेट लिंक करना होगा।
आम निवेशकों को इससे क्या 'बड़ा फायदा' मिलेगा?

फ्रैक्शनलाइजेशन (Fractionalisation - छोटे टुकड़ों में निवेश):अभी तक कॉरपोरेट बॉन्ड मार्केट मुख्य रूप से बड़े अमीर लोगों या संस्थाओं का खेल रहा है, क्योंकि एक-एक बॉन्ड की कीमत लाखों रुपये (जैसे ₹10 लाख न्यूनतम) होती है,Demat 2.0 और टोकनाइजेशन की मदद से इन बड़े बॉन्ड्स को ₹100 जैसे छोटे डिजिटल टोकन्स में तोड़ा जा सकेगा. यानी एक आम मध्यमवर्गीय व्यक्ति भी ₹100 या ₹500 से भारत की बड़ी कंपनियों के सुरक्षित बॉन्ड्स में निवेश कर सकेगा।

इंस्टेंट डिलीवरी और नो सेटलमेंट रिस्क:आज जब आप कोई बॉन्ड या शेयर खरीदते हैं, तो पैसे कटने और आपके अकाउंट में सिक्योरिटी आने के बीच समय का अंतर होता है. Demat 2.0 के Atomic Settlement की वजह से जैसे ही आप अपने CBDC वॉलेट से पेमेंट करेंगे, उसी माइक्रो-सेकंड में बॉन्ड आपके डीमैट खाते में आ जाएगा

ब्याज का ऑटोमैटिक क्रेडिट:चूंकि यह पूरा सिस्टम Smart Contracts (कोडिंग) पर चलेगा, इसलिए कंपनी कब ब्याज (Coupon) देगी, इसकी चिंता आपको नहीं करनी है,तय तारीख आते ही ब्लॉकचेन सिस्टम अपने आप आपके CBDC वॉलेट में ब्याज का पैसा ट्रांसफर कर देगा

भविष्य में इस व्यवस्था का दायरा केवल बॉन्ड्स तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा. तीसरे चरण में SEBI और RBI की योजना इसके तहत इक्विटी शेयर्स , म्यूचुअल फंड्स  और गोल्ड (Digital Gold Tokenisation) को भी शामिल करने की है।

5 developments stood out across markets and crypto today, spanning U.S. inflation, global capital flows, tokenized securities, perpetual markets and the growing connection between crypto and traditional finance.

🎙️U.S. consumer inflation accelerated in August. Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month and 3.4% year-on-year, while core CPI increased 0.3% MoM, above the 0.2% consensus, and stood at 2.4% YoY. Combined with yesterday's stronger PPI report, the data pushed market pricing for a 25 bp Federal Reserve hike next week to roughly 85%, from around 70% before CPI.

The bond market initially reinforced that message. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached approximately 4.99%, close to the psychologically important 5% level, before easing toward 4.92%. Bitcoin, meanwhile, continued trading around the $77,000 area, while oil retreated from an intraday Brent peak near $110 but remained above $100.

Market significance: The macro sequence is becoming increasingly difficult for risk assets to ignore. Stronger employment, higher producer inflation and now firmer consumer inflation are collectively giving the Fed considerably more room to tighten. Yet Bitcoin has not experienced a disorderly reaction. That does not make the current structure bullish, but it does mean the market is so far absorbing a substantial repricing of interest-rate expectations without a major leverage event. The next question is whether that stability survives if Treasury yields remain near 5%.

🎙️Global investors are simultaneously becoming more defensive. Equity funds recorded approximately $15.52B of net outflows in the week ending September 9, their largest weekly withdrawal since March. U.S. equity funds alone experienced approximately $32.27B of redemptions. At the same time, around $10.72B moved into money-market funds, while short-duration bond funds attracted approximately $6.65B.

Market significance: Crypto weakness is occurring inside a much broader reduction in risk appetite. Capital is not merely moving from Bitcoin into another part of crypto. Investors across conventional markets are shortening duration and moving toward instruments that offer liquidity and yield with less price risk. With risk-free yields approaching levels that can compete directly for capital, speculative assets face a progressively higher hurdle for attracting incremental money.

🎙️India has formally launched Demat 2.0, a joint RBI and SEBI pilot combining tokenized corporate securities, central-bank digital currency settlement and smart contracts. The first phase includes three corporate bond issuances involving Larsen & Toubro, REC and IIFL, with regulated institutions including CDSL, NSDL, BSE, NSE, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and NPCI participating in the broader architecture. The system is designed to enable faster settlement while automating parts of asset servicing such as interest payments and redemptions.

Market significance: This is considerably more important than simply issuing another tokenized bond. India is testing an architecture where the asset is tokenized, settlement occurs using central-bank money and the regulated financial system remains integrated throughout the process. If successfully extended into secondary trading and eventually other asset classes, tokenization begins affecting the actual plumbing of capital markets rather than remaining a parallel blockchain experiment.

🎙️Kalshi is seeking regulatory approval to introduce approximately 60 single-stock and ETF perpetual futures products in the United States, potentially including companies such as Apple, Nvidia and Tesla. Unlike conventional futures contracts, perpetuals have no fixed expiry and have historically been associated primarily with crypto markets. Kalshi has already introduced regulated perpetual products linked to crypto and precious metals.

Market significance: This represents an interesting reversal in the direction of financial innovation. Much of the tokenization discussion focuses on traditional assets moving onto crypto infrastructure. Perpetual futures show the opposite process taking place. A product structure developed and popularized within crypto markets is now being considered for conventional equities under U.S. regulation. Crypto is therefore influencing traditional market design, not merely receiving traditional assets.

🎙️The European Securities and Markets Authority has also warned that increasing connections between crypto and conventional finance create greater potential for interconnectedness and financial spillovers. ESMA highlighted growing tokenized-equity adoption, recent DeFi exploits and prediction markets while warning more broadly that deteriorating macroeconomic conditions and elevated valuations leave financial markets vulnerable to abrupt corrections.

Market significance: The regulatory concern itself is revealing. Historically, regulators were primarily concerned with losses occurring inside crypto markets. The discussion is increasingly shifting toward whether crypto has become connected enough to banks, securities markets, asset managers and payment infrastructure that instability could eventually move between the two systems. That concern only becomes relevant once integration reaches meaningful scale.

My Own Viewpoint:
Two processes are happening simultaneously, and separating them is becoming increasingly important.

Financial infrastructure is becoming more crypto-like while the macro environment is becoming less friendly to risk.

India is combining tokenized securities with central-bank money. Kalshi wants to bring perpetual futures into conventional equities. Regulators are beginning to discuss crypto in the context of financial-system interconnectedness.

These are structural developments. They do not disappear because Bitcoin falls a few percentage points.

But the other side of the market cannot be ignored.

Inflation remains persistent. The probability of another Federal Reserve hike has increased sharply. Treasury yields are challenging 5%. Oil remains above $100. Global investors are withdrawing money from equities and moving capital into money-market and shorter-duration instruments.

That means the opportunity cost of holding risk assets is rising at exactly the same time that crypto's underlying financial infrastructure is becoming more institutional.

This creates a distinction I think matters considerably:
Adoption and liquidity are not the same thing.

The infrastructure can continue improving while financial conditions suppress asset prices. Equally, weak prices do not automatically mean that the underlying adoption cycle has reversed.

For now, crypto's structural integration continues to advance, while the price of capital continues to move against it.

The market will eventually have to reconcile those two forces.

The price action over the last three sessions is perhaps even more interesting than the monthly numbers.

The basket gained 0.88% from Sep 7 to Sep 10, but the move was driven by a different set of names than the earlier leadership.

NEOGEN gained 8.2% and ORCHPHARMA 7.3%, while GUFICBIO, GOCOLORS and QPOWER pulled back.

The strongest cluster continues to be niche capital goods and pharma/CMO.

GMMPFAUDLR, QPOWER, SHILPAMED and SBCL continue to feature among the stronger performers. That clustering is interesting - the gains aren't coming from one isolated stock, but from a broader set of specialised businesses.

🎙️ Horizon Industrial Parks (HORIZONIND) call was streaming live on EquiSense, it just ended. Please find the summary below ⬇️
#ConcallInsights #DoubleDigitGrowth #MarginExpansion #CapacityExpansion #Logistics #Deleveraging

Can a company reporting a net loss of ₹12 crore actually be generating ₹116 crore of quarterly cash profit?

Horizon Industrial Parks reported its first post-listing numbers for Q1 FY27. Revenue reached ₹200 crore, up 23% YoY, while EBITDA expanded 36% to ₹161 crore with an 80% operating margin. Yet the bottom line printed a ₹12 crore loss.

The tension on the call was immediate: how quickly does the P&L reflect the company's transformed balance sheet?

Management explained that the reported loss is purely an accounting artifact of ₹75 crore non-cash depreciation and legacy interest costs. Following its ₹4,250 crore IPO capital raise, the company paid down ₹3,900 crore of debt, cutting pro forma net debt to ₹2,500 crore (12.5% of enterprise value). Factoring in those interest savings, pro forma quarterly cash profit stands at ₹116 crore, with accounting profit guided to turn positive by Q2/Q3 FY27.

Operationally, the engine is running fast. Horizon leased 1.9M sq ft in Q1—three-quarters to industrial manufacturing tenants at a 15-20% rental premium—taking its contracted revenue run-rate to ₹970 crore across 29.5M sq ft operational area. Full-year leasing is guided at 6.5M sq ft (~30% YoY growth), backed by a fully paid 2,300-acre land bank that can double capacity to 61M sq ft over 4-5 years.

Do the math on their expansion: Horizon plans ₹1,500-2,000 crore capex over 3 years. With internal accruals generating ~₹464 crore in annualized cash PAT against an equity funding ask of ~₹500-660 crore (1/3rd of capex), the buildout is comfortably self-funding.

However, a key friction point emerged in Q&A: 13 in-city warehouse tenders partnering with Central Warehousing Corporation are currently challenged in the Delhi High Court. Management cited sub-judice rules and declined to elaborate, even as they target a 13-14% yield on cost from that format.

Delivery of the maiden Pune in-city facility in Q4 FY27, resolution of the tender litigation, and accounting PAT turning black next quarter are the milestones to track.

That's the scoreboard to watch.

อินเดียเริ่มทดสอบโครงการนำร่องพันธบัตรแบบโทเคน (Tokenized Bond) มูลค่ารวม 107 ล้านดอลลาร์

หน่วยงานกำกับดูแลหลักทรัพย์และธนาคารกลางของอินเดีย ได้เปิดตัวโครงการนำร่องพันธบัตรองค์กรแบบโทเคนอย่างเป็นทางการ โดยมีบริษัท 3 แห่งร่วมออกพันธบัตรผ่านโครงสร้างพื้นฐานตลาดรูปแบบใหม่ รวมมูลค่า 1.025 หมื่นล้านรูปี หรือประมาณ 107 ล้านดอลลาร์สหรัฐ

เมื่อวันพฤหัสบดีที่ผ่านมา คณะกรรมการกำกับหลักทรัพย์และตลาดหลักทรัพย์ของอินเดีย หรือ SEBI ระบุว่าระบบ Demat 2.0 นี้ ช่วยให้สามารถออกและถือครองพันธบัตรองค์กรในรูปแบบโทเคนดิจิทัลบนบัญชีแยกประเภทแบบกระจายศูนย์ (Distributed Ledger) ซึ่งดูแลโดยหน่วยงานรับฝากหลักทรัพย์ของประเทศ โดยระบบนี้เชื่อมต่อกับสกุลเงินดิจิทัลของธนาคารกลาง (CBDC) ประเภทขายส่งของธนาคารกลางอินเดีย (RBI) ผ่านอินเทอร์เฟซตลาดแบบรวมศูนย์

การออกพันธบัตรครั้งแรกมาจาก REC ซึ่งเป็นผู้ให้กู้ภาครัฐ โดยระดมทุนได้ 5 พันล้านรูปีจากนักลงทุน 18 รายเมื่อวันจันทร์ที่ผ่านมา ตามด้วยบริษัทวิศวกรรมยักษ์ใหญ่ Larsen & Toubro (L&T) ที่ระดมทุนได้อีก 5 พันล้านรูปีจากนักลงทุน 4 รายในวันพุธ ส่วนผู้ให้กู้ที่ไม่ใช่ธนาคารอย่าง IIFL ได้ออกพันธบัตรมูลค่า 250 ล้านรูปีให้กับนักลงทุนรายหนึ่งในวันเดียวกัน

ทาง SEBI ระบุว่าโครงสร้างพื้นฐานนี้ช่วยให้ผู้ออกตราสารได้รับเงินทุนในวันที่เสนอราคาได้เลย แทนที่จะต้องรอ 2-3 วันเหมือนแต่ก่อน นอกจากนี้การชำระราคาแบบอะตอม (Atomic Settlement) ยังช่วยขจัดความล่าช้าในการโอนเงินและพันธบัตร ส่วนสัญญาอัจฉริยะ (Smart Contract) จะเข้ามาช่วยจัดการเรื่องการชำระดอกเบี้ยและการไถ่ถอนพันธบัตรให้เป็นไปโดยอัตโนมัติ

สำหรับแผนในระยะต่อไป SEBI จะเริ่มเปิดให้มีการซื้อขายในตลาดรองและเปิดโอกาสให้นักลงทุนรายย่อยสามารถเข้าถึงพันธบัตรแบบโทเคนเหล่านี้ได้ โดยจะนำประสบการณ์จากการทดสอบในระยะแรกมาปรับปรุงก่อนการเปิดใช้งานจริงในวงกว้างต่อไป ทั้งนี้ ราคา Bitcoin ในขณะนี้อยู่ที่ 77,000 ดอลลาร์ครับ

This SEBI Demat 2.0 pilot for tokenised corporate bonds feels like a big step, but I'm a little stuck on what it costs to not participate yet.

Three issuers have already put out ₹1,025 crore of these tokenised bonds. REC and L&T each did ₹500 crore, with REC’s going for 7.30% over about 20 months and L&T’s at 7.40% for three years. IIFL added ₹25 crore at a heftier 9.10% for two years. The tech uses DLT and RBI’s wholesale CBDC for settlement, which means the bond and money move together. That sounds like a solid defence against things going sideways.

What’s bugging me is the "pilot" part. This is all on a private DLT network, and Stage II, with secondary market trading and retail participation, is still in the works. For now, it's institutional investors only. If you’re an institutional investor, holding off seems fine while they iron out the kinks. But for the rest of us, the cost of doing nothing isn’t clear. What happens when this pilot rolls into Stage II, and the existing platforms connect to this DLT? Will holding onto older, non-tokenised bonds mean missed opportunities or higher transaction costs down the line? It's a real question I'd want answered before deciding anything.

INDIA JUST PUT CORPORATE BONDS ON THE BLOCKCHAIN

India has launched Demat 2.0, tokenizing corporate bonds and settling them using the RBI’s wholesale digital rupee.

💰 ₹1,025+ crore already tokenized in just one week:
* REC - ₹500 cr
* L&T - ₹500 cr
* IIFL Finance - ₹25 cr

The key upgrade? Atomic Delivery-vs-Payment (DvP) - the bond and digital rupee move together, enabling faster, same-day settlement and reducing settlement risk.

Smart contracts can also automate interest payments & redemptions.

But there’s a catch: no retail access and no live secondary market yet. The next big test is whether tokenized bonds can scale beyond this controlled institutional pilot.

India isn’t putting corporate debt on public crypto rails. It’s bringing blockchain + CBDC directly into regulated financial markets. 🚀

Sources: CoinDesk, The Crypto Times

据 CoinDesk 报道,印度证券交易委员会（SEBI）本周启动 Demat 2 试点，将公司债券以数字代币形式发行在受监管市场机构运行的分布式账本上，并通过印度储备银行的批发数字卢比完成结算。印度公司债市场规模约 6200 亿美元。

国有电力贷款机构 REC 通过该系统融资 500 亿卢比（约 5600 万美元），工程与建筑巨头 Larsen & Toubro 再融资 500 亿卢比，非银贷款机构 IIFL Finance 融资 25 亿卢比（约 280 万美元），合计约 1025 亿卢比。债券仍保留固定利率、到期日和投资者权利，但代币化债券与用于购买的数字卢比可同步结算，从而降低交易风险。

后续阶段将引入智能合约处理付息与赎回等公司行动，并计划开放二级市场交易，最终向散户投资者开放。印度对私人加密货币态度谨慎，此次试点是将代币化引入其已掌控的金融体系。

₹1,025 crore of corporate bonds from REC, L&T and IIFL Finance are using permissioned DLT, not a public chain like Ethereum.

So this isn’t DeFi.

🚨🇮🇳 BREAKING: India’s Bond Market Is Entering the Blockchain Era — DEMAT 2.0

भारत ने अपने financial market infrastructure में एक बड़ा technological leap लिया है।

(SEBI) और  (RBI) ने “Demat 2.0” pilot शुरू किया है, जिसका उद्देश्य corporate bonds को tokenised securities के रूप में issue, hold और settle करना है।

🔹 Blockchain / Distributed Ledger Technology पर securities का digital record
🔹 Settlement के लिए RBI का Wholesale Digital Rupee (e₹-W)
🔹 Smart contracts के जरिए interest payment और redemption जैसे processes को automate करने की क्षमता
🔹 Atomic Delivery-versus-Payment — यानी bond और payment का settlement एक साथ
🔹 Faster settlement, बेहतर transparency और reconciliation risk को कम करने की संभावना।

💰 Pilot में अब तक:

🏦 REC — ₹500 करोड़
🏗️ L&T — ₹500 करोड़
💼 IIFL Finance — ₹25 करोड़

यानी कुल ₹1,025 करोड़ के tokenised corporate bonds इस pilot ecosystem में शामिल हैं।

सबसे महत्वपूर्ण बात यह है कि यह सिर्फ “crypto” की कहानी नहीं है।

यह दिखाता है कि blockchain technology अब regulated financial markets, corporate debt और institutional settlement infrastructure में भी वास्तविक उपयोग के लिए अपनाई जा रही है।

अभी pilot का focus institutional participation पर है। Secondary-market trading और wider retail participation आगे के phases में expand किए जाने की योजना है।

🇮🇳 India is not just experimenting with blockchain anymore — it is beginning to build regulated financial infrastructure around it.

Demat 1.0 digitised securities.
Demat 2.0 could make securities programmable, tokenised and digitally settled.

Personal view: This is India's strategic move to control its digital financial evolution. Rather than open blockchains, regulators are building a permissioned, integrated system. It’s a "walled garden" tokenization, keeping banks and central bank money at its core. This contrasts with broader Web3 ethos but ensures regulatory oversight and stability, a pragmatic state-backed evolution.

Small and Midcaps have a much smaller free float and that leads to a scarcity bubble in that space...!

Good businesses available at insane valuations....!

Also there aren't enough themes to play in the Indian markets. 

The themes that have played out in the last 10 years

1. Speciality Chemicals
2. PSU rerating 
3. Defence 
4. Discretionary consumption - hospitality, QSR, Retail
5. EMS 
6. Financial "utilities" - AMCs, RTAs, Depositories & Exchanges
7. CDMO
8. Diagnostics
9. Hi-tech Engineering - Sedemac, Indo MIM varieties
10. Railways - I have my reservations though

Except for Hi-tech,none of them are really "Sun rise" sectors actually. They've only been "Discovered". Also the companies in the space do not have the ability to absorb liquidity, this causes the valuations to stay stretched. For the Indian markets to absorb this 30k SIP and delivery returns meaningfully, the breadth and depth of the markets have to increase or else we will have too much money chasing too few stocks leading to bubbles.

INDIA'S FIRST TOKENIZED CORPORATE BONDS GO LIVE

-India just put more than ₹1,025 crore of ordinary corporate debt onto tokenized rails in one week.REC raised ₹500 crore at 7.30% on Sept 7. L&T followed with ₹500 crore at 7.40%, becoming the first private issuer. IIFL Finance added ₹25 crore at 9.10%, the first non-PSU NBFC deal.

-These are still regular rupee bonds. Credit risk, coupons, and legal claims have not moved onto a public chain. What changed is settlement: bidding stayed on NSE’s electronic platform, holdings were recorded on NSDL and CDSL Demat 2.0, and cash moved through wholesale CBDC wallets with same-day atomic delivery versus payment.

-The catch is the market around them. The notes are listed, but there is still no live secondary trading venue; retail access is closed, and only institutions with both a Demat 2.0 wallet and a wholesale e₹ wallet can participate. Exchanges have been expected to build a trading layer later this year.

-The bonds are live. The market is not.

The real takeaway isn't cans versus bottles.

It's that smart consumer companies now treat packaging as a strategic lever, not an afterthought. 

The ones building flexibility into their supply chain today are the ones festive season won't catch off guard.

That's how businesses actually get built to last.

Here's the sharpest bit. For beer, prices are capped by the state, unlike soft drinks.

So brewers can't simply pass on higher costs to consumers. 

They're absorbing it instead, while waiting out the storm.

Glass brings its own equation. It needs industrial gas to manufacture, and it's heavier and more fragile to transport.

So this isn't a free swap. 

It's a trade-off between packaging types, not a total escape from rising costs.

So beverage and alcohol companies did what any smart business does when one channel narrows.

They diversified. Faster shift to glass and PET bottles to keep shelves stocked for the festive rush.

On top of that, India tightened safety and quality norms for imported aluminium sheets this year.

Good for standards. But it also meant fewer suppliers could legally sell into India right now.

More friction, right as festive season demand was picking up.

Naturally, prices flew up. Nearly 25% higher than last year at one point.

India felt this hard. 

We're the world's second largest aluminium producer, but we don't make enough of the specific thin, food-grade sheet that beverage cans need.

We import most of it.

Making aluminium needs huge amounts of electricity and raw material shipped in by sea.

The crisis disrupted both for Gulf producers. Smelters shut down. Ships couldn't move through the Strait of Hormuz.

Nearly 9% of the world's aluminium supply took a hit, almost overnight.

So China capped how much aluminium it produces every year.

The world still had other suppliers to lean on. A shortage was expected, but a small, manageable one.

Then came the West Asia crisis.

It starts in China.

China makes nearly 60% of the world's aluminium. 

Late 2024, it pulled back a tax benefit that made its aluminium cheap for the rest of the world.

Why? China wants to use more of its own aluminium to build higher-value products, not just export raw metal.

Earlier this year, Diet Coke cans quietly vanished from stores in Indian metros.

Not the drink. Just the can.

The real story behind this has nothing to do with Coca-Cola. 

It starts on the other side of the world.

WHY KEEP AN EYE ON THE NIFTY SME EMERGE UNIVERSE?
The interesting part of the SME segment is that many businesses are still in the expansion phase - adding capacity, entering new markets, building customers and scaling their operations.

But this also means higher risk.
So, don't simply look at a stock because it is part of the Nifty SME Emerge universe or because its price has performed well.

For every company, we should study:
▪️ Business model & industry opportunity
▪️ Revenue and earnings growth
▪️ Balance sheet
▪️ Cash-flow generation
▪️ Debt & working capital
▪️ ROE / ROCE
▪️ Promoter holding & pledge
▪️ Order book and order inflow
▪️ Capacity & utilisation
▪️ Capex plans
▪️ Customer concentration
▪️ Annual reports
▪️ Quarterly results
▪️ Concalls / investor presentations
▪️ Corporate announcements
▪️ Management quality
▪️ Valuation
▪️ Technical structure & liquidity

The Nifty SME Emerge index itself has at least 20 constituents, with eligibility requiring NSE Emerge listing and a minimum trading frequency at quarterly review; constituents are weighted by free-float market capitalisation.

So the objective here is simple:
Don't chase the stock.
Study the business.
Track the execution.

Through print media monitoring and media intelligence, this press review covers eight essential blockchain and Web3 stories. According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, these stories capture the news on blockchain and Web3 shaping India's digital economy — from central bank experiments to state-level tokenisation and regulatory enforcement.

1. FIU-IND Issues Compliance Notices to 15 Crypto Platforms
A front-page report in Economic Times says the Financial Intelligence Unit-India has issued compliance notices to 15 virtual digital asset service providers for allegedly violating the country's anti-money laundering framework. The regulator also directed action to take down the applications and URLs of these entities from public access, invoking its powers as the nodal authority under the Information Technology Act and related intermediary rules. The platforms named include Weex, Blofin, Rezorex, Bitunix, DigiFinex, Toobit, https://t.co/a7U0L7NZR6, Latoken, WOO X, Pionex, ChangeNow, SimpleSwap, FixedFloat, WhiteBIT and Guardarian.

Why it matters: Unregistered platforms operating without PMLA compliance pose systemic risks to India's financial ecosystem. The action signals zero tolerance for offshore exchanges targeting Indian users.

Key detail: Platforms named include Weex, Blofin, Rezorex, Bitunix, DigiFinex, Toobit, https://t.co/a7U0L7NZR6, Latoken, WOO X, Pionex, ChangeNow, SimpleSwap, FixedFloat, WhiteBIT, and Guardarian.

Source: Economic Times, front-page report.

Next step: Expect stricter KYC and reporting requirements for all VDA service providers operating in India. Tag @FIU_IND and @EconomicTimes in your comments on this enforcement action.

2. Maharashtra to Tokenise Land Assets via DELTA Act
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says Maharashtra will become the first state in India to tokenise land using blockchain technology, aiming to unlock the full value of property and enhance liquidity in the real estate market. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced the proposed Maharashtra Digitisation and Exchange of Land Token Asset Act at the Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai on Wednesday, with the framework being developed with inputs from SEBI, BSE, NSE, and experts from industry, technology, law, and academia. Land assets covered under the new framework are estimated to be worth fifty lakh crore rupees.

Why it matters: Tokenising land assets could transform India's real estate market by enhancing liquidity and enabling fractional ownership through blockchain technology.

Key detail: The framework is being developed with inputs from SEBI, BSE, NSE, and experts from industry, technology, law, and academia. Land assets covered are estimated to be worth fifty lakh crore rupees.

Source: Hindustan Times, front-page report.

Next step: Watch for legislative drafting and stakeholder consultations in the coming months. Tag @DevendraFadnavis and @HindustanTimes if this impacts your real estate portfolio.

3. RBI Explores Gold Tokenisation on Unified Markets Interface
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says the Reserve Bank of India is exploring gold tokenisation on its Unified Markets Interface, which settles tokenised financial instruments using central bank digital currency. RBI Executive Director P. Vasudevan announced this during a fireside chat at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on September 9, noting that the central bank has already tested the platform with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth Rs 17,000 crore.

Why it matters: Gold tokenisation on a CBDC-settled platform could reshape commodity trading and bring transparency to India's gold market.

Key detail: The RBI has already tested tokenisation with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth Rs 17,000 crore.

Source: Deccan Chronicle, front-page report.

Next step: Expect pilot expansions to other asset classes in the near term. Tag @RBI and @DeccanChronicle if you follow fintech innovation.

4. RBI Settles Tokenised Financial Instruments Using CBDC
A front-page report in Asian Age says the Reserve Bank of India settled tokenised financial instruments using central bank digital currency. The RBI tested tokenisation with 248 certificate-of-deposit transactions worth twenty-one thousand seven hundred crore rupees. RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain and Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri highlighted challenges and economic priorities at the event.

Why it matters: CBDC-settled tokenisation bridges the gap between traditional finance and blockchain-based markets, reducing settlement risk and increasing efficiency.

Key detail: RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain and Niti Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri highlighted challenges and economic priorities at the event.

Source: Asian Age, front-page report.

Next step: Monitor how other central banks respond to India's progress in CBDC-based settlement. Tag @RBI and @NITIAayog for their leadership in digital finance.

5. RBI Expands UMI Tokenisation to New Asset Classes
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says the recently launched night service buses branded as Third Shift in Greater Hyderabad have drawn a strong response, with 9,286 passengers using them in the first seven days. The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation is now planning to extend operations to a 24x7 service, with more night routes to be added soon. The corporation introduced the special services on September 1 across six major routes in the Greater Hyderabad zone, targeting the IT corridor and high-traffic areas after a departmental study.

Why it matters: Expanding UMI to more asset classes could democratise access to tokenised investments for millions of Indian retail investors.

Key detail: NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri emphasized India's need to scale manufacturing, while UIDAI chairperson Neelkanth Mishra noted Aadhaar's expanding authentication capacity.

Source: Deccan Chronicle, front-page report.

Next step: Watch for regulatory clarity on data privacy and legal frameworks for tokenised assets. Tag @RBI and @UIDAI as these frameworks evolve.

6. L&T and IIFL Finance Enter Tokenised Bond Market
A front-page report in Business Standard says Larsen & Toubro and IIFL Finance entered India's tokenised bond market this week, raising Rs 500 crore and Rs 25 crore respectively. REC had earlier completed the first such issuance, raising Rs 750 crore through a 20-month bond. The framework uses blockchain technology and the Reserve Bank of India's central bank digital currency for settlement.

Why it matters: Tokenised bonds offer faster settlement, greater transparency, and broader investor access — key advantages for India's capital markets.

Key detail: REC had earlier completed the first such issuance, raising Rs 750 crore through a 20-month bond. The framework uses blockchain technology and RBI's central bank digital currency for settlement.

Source: Business Standard, front-page report.

Next step: Expect more corporates to follow suit as the tokenised bond market matures. Tag @LarsenToubro and @IIFLFinance for their pioneering role.

7. 25 Offshore Crypto Exchanges Served Legal Notices in 2025
A front-page report in Economic Times says the Indian government issued notices in 2025 to 25 offshore cryptocurrency exchanges for non-compliance under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Platforms such as Huione, Paxful, Changelly and BitMex were catering to Indian users without registering with the Financial Intelligence Unit of India. These offshore exchanges operated from various jurisdictions worldwide but actively solicited Indian users without ensuring compliance with Indian financial laws.

Why it matters: Offshore exchanges operating without Indian regulatory oversight expose users to significant financial and legal risks.

Key detail: These exchanges operated from various jurisdictions worldwide but actively solicited Indian users without ensuring compliance with Indian financial laws.

Source: Economic Times, front-page report.

Next step: The 2025 enforcement wave sets the stage for continued scrutiny of cross-border crypto operations. Tag @EconomicTimes and @FIU_IND for their enforcement efforts.

8. Rs 113 Crore Crypto Fraud Arrested in UAE
A front-page report in Times of India says Lakhanpal, who allegedly posed as a finance ministry official, was arrested in the UAE for defrauding investors of more than Rs 113 crore through a fake money trade coin cryptocurrency scheme in 2017-18. The Enforcement Directorate shared his whereabouts with Thane police, leading to his arrest on September 1, after which the government initiated extradition proceedings. Investigators also found a police officer in Thane handled his office and clients, and Lakhanpal had fled India after acquiring Antigua and Barbuda passports.

Why it matters: The arrest demonstrates India's commitment to pursuing crypto fraudsters across borders and protecting investors from sophisticated scams.

Key detail: Investigators found a police officer in Thane handled his office and clients, and Lakhanpal had fled India after acquiring Antigua and Barbuda passports.

Source: Times of India, front-page report.

Next step: The extradition process will be closely watched as a test case for international crypto fraud prosecution. Tag @TimesOfIndia and @EnforcementDirectorate for their investigative work.

India’s New Industrial Revolution is already being rewarded.
Jefferies highlighted Space, Semiconductors & Electronics, Data Centers, Solar Manufacturing and Aerospace as the next big growth engines.
The stock market has taken notice — and in several cases is pricing the opportunity well ahead of the Nifty 50.
Here’s the clear scorecard:
Aerospace & Defence (incl. Space ecosystem)
The strongest performer.
Nifty India Defence has decisively beaten the Nifty 50 across 1-year and multi-year periods.
HAL, BEL, MTAR Technologies, Data Patterns, Astra Microwave, Sansera Engineering and Azad Engineering have delivered standout returns.
Global OEMs (Boeing & Airbus) are steadily increasing Indian sourcing. Pure space startups remain private — so listed suppliers are capturing the re-rating.
Data Centers
The AI infrastructure trade is very much alive in India.
Related names in optical fibre, power, cooling and transformers have added tens of billions in market value even as broader indices lagged.
Sterlite Technologies and HFCL turned multi-baggers on hyperscaler demand. Power-equipment and precision cooling plays (CG Power, Hitachi Energy, MTAR) are also clear beneficiaries.
Solar Manufacturing
India is already the world’s No. 2 solar PV manufacturer.
Capacity is scaling rapidly and localisation is heading toward ~90% of the value chain by 2030.
Premier Energies, Waaree Energies, Emmvee and peers have posted strong revenue and profit growth. Returns remain solid, though more selective after the earlier rally.
Semiconductors & Electronics
Still early-stage.
Policy has moved from intent to execution ($20 bn+ pipeline + fresh incentives). Gains are showing more in electronics manufacturing and component plays than pure semiconductor names so far.
Versus Nifty 50
While the benchmark has been range-bound or modest, these thematic pockets have delivered clear relative outperformance — classic behaviour when structural themes gain visibility.
Will the growth continue?
Yes — on a multi-year structural basis.
Policy support is broad (space sector opening, data-centre tax holidays, PLI schemes, localisation mandates). Domestic demand is rising. Global China+1, AI build-out and aerospace supply-chain shifts all favour India. Order books and capacity under construction give multi-year visibility.
Risks remain: elevated valuations, execution delays, and limited pure-play listed options in space and advanced semis. Volatility will stay high.

Har engine ke andar ek aisi cheez hoti hai jise koi nahi dekhta.

Engine bearing. Crankshaft aur connecting rod ke beech ki patli layer. Micron level ki precision. Ghiste rehna uska kaam hai, taaki engine na ghise.

Kolhapur ki Menon Bearings yahi banati hai — bearings, bushes, thrust washers. Saath mein aluminium die-casting (Alkop) aur braking components. Customers mein Maruti, Mahindra, Cummins, Kirloskar, Eicher. Exports UK, Spain, Israel aur USA tak.

Q1 FY27:

Revenue ₹91.79 crore, 36.57% up. Highest-ever quarter.
Consolidated PAT ₹14.11 crore, 67.38% up.
PBT ₹18.51 crore, 67.4% up.
₹2 per share interim dividend, saal ke beech mein.

Ab do cheezein jo headline ke neeche hain.

Pehli — margin.

Other income hataakar operating margin 21.92% rahi. Q4 FY26 mein 24.79% thi. Karib 287 basis point sequentially neeche.

Revenue record pe, margin peak se peeche. Company ne khud bataya ki production badhne se cost badhe.

Doosri — aur yeh zyada interesting hai.

Consolidated PAT ₹14.11 crore, standalone ₹11.23 crore. Farak ₹2.88 crore — subsidiary ka hissa.

Sequential dekhiye. Standalone Q4 ke ₹9.50 crore se ₹11.23 crore — 18% up. Par consolidated ₹13.78 crore se ₹14.11 crore — sirf 2.4%.

Matlab parent tez badhi, subsidiary sequentially gira. Ek hi result mein do alag directions.

Ab structural baat.

Engine bearing, bush, thrust washer — yeh sab engine ke parts hain. EV mein engine hi nahi hota. Yaani is company ka content per vehicle EV share badhne ke saath ghatega. Tyre ya glass ki tarah fuel-agnostic nahi.

Abhi problem nahi hai. India mein bikne wali zyadatar gaadiyon mein engine hai — CNG aur hybrid dono mein bhi. Demand strong hai.

Par direction ek hi taraf hai.

Capacity badhi hai — Bi-Metal 486 se 580 lakh units, Brakes 30 se 50 lakh pieces.

Jo dhyan mein rakhna hai:

EV diversification abhi early stage hai. 8-10% target hai, achieved nahi.
Auto sector cyclical hai. 36% growth strong base pe repeat karna mushkil.
Margin peak se peeche. Agle do quarter batayenge ki 24.79% high tha ya 21.92% naya normal.
Subsidiary ka sequential girna ek quarter ki baat hai ya trend, abhi saaf nahi.
Company chhoti hai. Scale, raw material aur forex ka exposure rating agency khud flag kar chuki.

Takeaway:

Har business ke apne support aur resistance hote hain — price mein nahi, numbers mein.

Menon ke liye support hai capacity, jo abhi badhi. Resistance hai margin, jo 24.79% se 21.92% pe aa gayi.

Aur ek lamba structural resistance — engine ka future.

Aaj engine hai, isliye business chal raha hai. Sawaal yeh ki jab engine kam honge, tab kya hoga.

Company ka jawab teen hisson mein hai. Alkop ke through EV components — target hai FY27 tak Alkop revenue ka 8-10% EV se aaye. Braking division, jo powertrain-neutral hai — brake har gaadi mein lagta hai. Aur Menon Bearings New Ventures, jo EV charging aur cold chain explore kar rahi hai.

Teenon abhi chhote hain. Par yehi teen track karne layak hain — inhi se pata chalega ki jawab kaam kar raha hai ya sirf plan hai.

Bottom line:

India's first GLP-1 opportunity was obvious:

Make semaglutide cheaper and sell more of it.

The next opportunity could be much deeper:

Manufacture the API, fill the injection and produce it for dozens of brands globally.

But this won't be easy money.

Peptide manufacturing is difficult.

Quality problems can delay launches, while 40+ brands can destroy pricing power quickly.

Then there’s the API opportunity.

Companies that can reliably manufacture peptide APIs can supply multiple brands instead of competing with them.

That means the GLP-1 opportunity could spread across:
API → Formulation → Fill-finish → Injector → CDMO

And we’re already seeing evidence of this.

OneSource supported a generic semaglutide programme that received tentative US FDA approval.

It has also supported approvals in Canada.

That changes the economics completely.

Imagine 40 pharma companies fighting to sell semaglutide.

The company manufacturing for 5–10 of them doesn't need to know which brand ultimately wins.

Why?
Semaglutide isn't a simple tablet.

It's a complex peptide that needs specialised manufacturing, sterile filling and reliable injector devices.

To understand where the real value could sit, break one injection into 3 layers:

Formulation - selling the medicine
API - manufacturing the peptide
CDMO - manufacturing for other pharma companies

And that creates a strange situation.

Demand for GLP-1 drugs is exploding.

But if 40+ brands are selling essentially the same molecule, competition can quickly push prices and margins down.

First, what changed?

On March 20, semaglutide's key patent expired in India.

Natco launched at just Rs.1,290/month, while companies like Sun, Dr Reddy's, Zydus, Alkem and Torrent entered the race.

Suddenly, a very expensive drug became a crowded generic market.

One of the world's biggest drugs just lost patent protection in India.

Within days, 40+ companies were ready with versions of semaglutide.

But the biggest opportunity may NOT be selling the injection.

It may be manufacturing what goes inside it. 👇

Park Medi World 

CMP: 282
MCAP: 12193 cr
P/E: 43.9

Park Medi World Limited, which runs the Park Group of Hospitals, has just set up a brand new company that it owns completely. This new company is called Park Medicity Prayagraj Limited, and it officially came into existence on September 8, 2026.

The reason they created this new entity is to build and run a large hospital in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. This will be a 550 bed multi super speciality hospital, meaning it will offer many different medical specialities under one roof.

Interestingly, this hospital project has come through a public private partnership, which means the local municipal corporation in Prayagraj has awarded this project to Park Medi World to build and operate the hospital, rather than the government building it entirely on its own.

Since Park Medi World owns one hundred percent of this new company, there is no conflict of interest here. No related parties or group companies have any special stake in this deal, and everything has been done at arm's length, meaning fairly and without favoritism.

The amount of money involved to start this new subsidiary is quite small at this stage, only about fifteen lakh rupees, used to buy one lakh fifty thousand shares in the new company. This is essentially just the initial seed capital needed to officially register the new entity. 

The bigger investment for actually building the hospital would likely come later.

This move signals that Park Medi World is expanding its footprint beyond its existing markets into a new and significant city. 

Prayagraj is a major religious and administrative hub in Uttar Pradesh, known for large events like the Kumbh Mela which draw enormous crowds, so a large modern hospital there could serve a very large population base that may currently lack access to advanced medical care.

Winning a public private partnership project is also meaningful because governments usually award such contracts only to companies they consider financially capable and credible, so it can be seen as a vote of confidence in Park Medi World's ability to execute large scale healthcare projects. 

Successfully completing this one could also make it easier for the company to win similar hospital contracts in other cities in the future, creating a template for growth through government partnerships rather than only through fully self funded new hospitals.

From a business perspective, once operational, a 550 bed hospital adds a large amount of new bed capacity to the company's overall network, which over the years should translate into a meaningful boost to revenue and profits as the hospital ramps up patient volumes. It also allows Park Medi World to diversify geographically, reducing its dependence on its current cities and giving it a foothold in a fast growing part of Uttar Pradesh.

However, since actual construction, government approvals, staffing, and eventually filling up hospital beds with patients typically take several years, the real financial benefit from this move will likely show up gradually over the coming years rather than immediately. 

In short, this is a long term growth seed being planted today, positioning the company for expanded scale and geographic reach in the healthcare sector over the next several years.

WHY HEALTHCARE CAN BE INTERESTING
The interesting part of healthcare is that revenue can be repeat in nature, depending on the business.

▪️ Hospitals → patients continuously require treatments, procedures and healthcare services.

▪️ Diagnostics → tests are performed repeatedly, creating recurring demand.

▪️ Pharma → chronic therapies and regularly prescribed medicines can provide repeat business.

▪️ Medical devices & consumables → many products are consumed or require replacement, creating repeat demand.

▪️ CDMO / contract manufacturing → once a company develops a relationship with a customer, repeat orders can potentially create long-term revenue visibility.

▪️ Healthcare platforms & services → established customer/patient networks can create recurring usage and stronger operating leverage as the business scales.

But recurring revenue doesn't automatically mean a good investment.

We still need to check the quality of the revenue, margins, cash flows, debt, working capital, customer concentration, regulatory risks, promoter quality and valuation.

Healthcare can be a very powerful compounding sector - but only when the underlying business, execution and valuation all make sense.

So don't just look at which stock has gone up.
Study the business. Track the execution. Research the numbers. Then take a decision.
